title: Registry Entry Exists, Summary Not Found
claim: The v0.10.0 release is published and closed: registry, schema, code documents, examples, checker, and tests are all consistent and independently verified.

observed_evidence.detail: The registry declares eighteen defined codes, and the schema code enum contains the identical eighteen. Both are machine-parsed, not read from prose.
The document section headed 'Registry summary' carries sixteen table rows. Two published codes have no row; a git history search finds no commit that ever added one.
The publication commit edited that same table to add the newest code's row and rewrote the surrounding set prose, so the summary was in scope and reaffirmed, not merely untouched.
The section is headed 'Registry summary' with no 'selected', 'partial', or 'examples only' qualifier, and the prose two lines below restates the full contiguous defined set correctly.
Publication closure is asserted for the release, and the published ref matches the local ref with no divergence.

missing_evidence.detail: No surface compares the public summary row set to the canonical defined set. The integrity checker reads the document only as a relative-link resolution target.
Two published canonical codes have no representation in the document most readers treat as the registry.

required_action: Block publication closure, not the published bytes. Add the missing rows to the summary using titles and default effects taken from the registry rather than re-authored. Add a deterministic parity check that parses the canonical defined set and the summary row set and fails on any missing or extra member, covered by an adversarial tamper test. Re-freeze and independently review the repaired bytes: PREVIOUS_VERIFIER_PASS is not PASS_FOR_MUTATED_BYTES. Do not remove the canonical entries, roll back the codes, or claim the implementation or the release is absent.

scope_isolation.detail: Sibling projections were correct at the observed commit, which is evidence against an intentionally-partial reading and bounds the required repair to one table.

detection_gap.checker_does_not_enforce: summary table row set vs canonical defined set

notes: Derived from an observed episode in this repository; the defect was in the projection only, and the canonical bytes were correct throughout. Provenance of the underlying set comparison is PRIMARY_PERSISTED — committed bytes machine-parsed on both sides — while narrative details are omitted rather than reconstructed. No commit id, digest, path, or timestamp is asserted here as canonical fact. ENTRY_PRESENT_IN_REGISTRY does not imply ENTRY_PRESENT_TO_THE_READER. The author of the release also recorded the defect, which is a reason for independent review of these bytes, not a reason to soften the record.
